title: After a sin
hookLine: all children of Adam err, and the best of them repent (Tirmidhi)
tomorrow: how did a father wait for a son he thought was gone?

lines: THE THING SAID IN THE KITCHEN.
cards: The thing said in the kitchen, in a voice you'd never use on a stranger, to the person who'd do anything for you.
Then the second hard part, which can be worse: the replay, the shame, the urge to avoid her eyes for a week. So what does anyone do after doing wrong?
It's one of the oldest questions people ask, and this tradition's answer starts with a family name.

teach.b: The Prophet ﷺ put it plainly, in Tirmidhi: every child of Adam errs, and the best of those who err are those who repent. Not the ones who never fall; that list is empty. The best are the ones who come back.

In the Qur'an, Adam and his wife eat from the tree, and their first words afterward aren't excuses: "Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If thou forgive us not and have not mercy on us, surely we are of the lost!"
Name it, own it, turn back.

teach.h: TWO DOORS: TO GOD, AND TO HER.
teach.b: And the door stays wide: "Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins." When the wrong landed on a person, there's a second door.
The Prophet said whoever has wronged someone should make it right with them today. So tawba after a cruel word runs two ways: to God, and to her. Here's something shared with a neighbor.
The Hebrew Bible says it too, in an older Jewish translation: "For there is not a righteous man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not."
Jewish tradition calls the way back teshuvah, return, and the Mishnah teaches that a wrong against another person waits on that person's forgiveness too.

One honest difference: Jewish tradition also gives return a season each year, the Days of Awe, ending in Yom Kippur, prayed together as a congregation. The hadith names no season; its door is open on any ordinary night.

how: Muslims repent (tawba) by stopping the wrong, regretting it, resolving not to return to it and asking Allah's forgiveness, often saying astaghfirullah; when a person was wronged, they also seek that person's pardon and set things right.

o: a wrong so serious that it can't be forgiven
a wrong kept secret so that no one is hurt
turning back after a wrong, to God and the one hurt

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.
p: Adam's first words after the tree

s: in the hadith, the best people are the ones who never sin
every child of Adam errs; the best of those who err are those who repent.
after wronging a person, the Prophet said to make it right with them
tawba after a cruel word runs two ways: to God, and to the person.
Ecclesiastes, like the hadith, says no one is without sin
'there is not a righteous man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.'

games.q: a coworker took credit for your idea last month. now he quietly admits it and says he's 'just not a good person.' what fits today's hadith?
o: every child of Adam errs; the best of them return, and he's returning.
good believers don't do that, so his faith must be weak.
he only owes God an apology; he doesn't owe you anything.
games.why: the hadith doesn't sort people into good and bad; it says everyone errs, and the best come back, to God and to the person wronged.

practice: Close your eyes and bring back one wrong that's still sitting with you. Don't replay the scene; just name it plainly, the way Adam did.

If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah, I ask Allah's forgiveness, slowly, a few times; if not, breathe with the name of it. Before you open your eyes, picture the first small step toward the person, if there is one.

wordCard.voice: After a sin: every child of Adam errs. The best of them return, to God, and to whoever they hurt.

orig.note: Arabic: repentance; turning back to God after a wrong.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: the best return, for every child of Adam who falls. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2499 (every son of Adam errs; the best of those who err are those who repent)

Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins.
